newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close at year high on firm ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close at year high on firm ADRs.

text.p: Argentine blue chips, continuing the firm trend of recent sessions, closed Monday at the year's high on the back of stronger Argentine ADR prices, dealers said.
"After the strong rise in domestic stocks, the market reinforced its rally on strong purchases of Argentine firms that quote in the U.S. market," said Jorge Bonanno of Interfin brokers.
The blue chip index MerVal closed 1.87 percent higher at 628.62 points, breaking its previous highest level of 619.37 posted on May 21.
Volume rose to $24 million from Friday's $17.7 million.
"Today was a key session," Bonanno said. "In the first part of the day foreign markets were declining heavily but Argentine ADRs showed no decliners."
"A better tax collection in November was a fresh cue for buyers who pushed the Merval up," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro y Ca.
Dealers see the upward trend continuing in the next sessions.
"The market is starting the week on the rise," said Gustavo Galfione of Velox Inversiones. "The trend may continue for the next few days considering the good performance of ADRs."
The broader general index rose 0.87 percent, with gainers beating losers by 41 to 10 and 16 shares flat.
The best performances among main tiers were textile and footware Alpargatas with an 8.5 percent rise and paper-maker Celulosa up 7.9 percent.
